name.text: Shared: Convert standard form to a large number

questiontext.text:
Write \[ {@coefficient_display@} \times 10^{@exponent@} \] as an ordinary whole number.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

A positive power of \(10\) moves the decimal point to the right.

Starting from \[ {@coefficient_display@}, \] move the decimal point \[ {@exponent@} \] places to the right.

Therefore, \[ \boxed{{@answer@}}. \]

prtincorrect.text: For a positive power of \(10\), move the decimal point to the right.

node.description: Checks whether the decimal point was moved in the wrong direction.

truefeedback.text:
You moved the decimal point in the wrong direction.

Because the exponent is positive, multiply by a power of \(10\), so the decimal point moves to the right.

node.description: Checks whether the decimal point was moved one place too few.

truefeedback.text:
Your direction is correct, but you moved the decimal point one place too few.

The exponent tells you the total number of places to move.

falsefeedback.text: Use the exponent to count how many places the decimal point moves to the right.

qtest.description: Moving the decimal point in the wrong direction receives zero credit.
Moving the decimal point one place too few receives zero credit.
